newsitem.title: USA: New York police shakeup after alleged attack.
newsitem.headline: New York police shakeup after alleged attack.

text.p: Top police officers were reassigned on Thursday in a shakeup at a police precinct where a Haitian immigrant was allegedly beaten and sodomized with a toilet plunger.
The immigrant, Abner Louima, remained in a hospital in critical and guarded condition after the alleged attack Saturday at the precinct in the city's Brooklyn borough.
Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, who announced the shakeup at a City Hall news conference, warned police at the 70th Precinct not protect their fellow officers behind a so-called blue wall of silence.

"We want more cooperation.... If they search their conscience and their soul and they're not capable of doing that, they should take their badge and turn it in and go do something else for a living," he said. "We don't want them in the police department."
Louima, 30, told investigators he was arrested in a late-night brawl outside a nightclub, pushed to the ground, handcuffed, kicked and beaten.
He said officers told him: "You niggers have to learn to respect police officers."
He said he was taken to the stationhouse, where he was sodomized with a toilet plunger handle. He said the officers also shoved it into his mouth and smashed his teeth.
He has undergone surgery for a pierced rectum and torn bladder. He also suffered a fractured jaw, underwent a colostomy and faces more surgery, doctors at Coney Island Hospital said.

Giuliani announced that the top two officers at the 70th Precinct -- the commanding officer and the executive officer -- were reassigned. Another 10 officers, including the supervising desk sergeant, were placed on modified assignment or suspended. One officer was suspended on Wednesday.
Another officer, Justin Volpe, was arraigned on criminal charges of aggravated sexual abuse and assault.
